industry.headline: TikTok Reaches First State Settlement Over Teen Safety, Agrees to Usage Limits and Age Verification
industry.summary: TikTok settled with Alabama ahead of the first state trial over teen mental health harms, agreeing to pay $100M+ and adopt usage limits and age verification — a template regulators in NOMO's core US/UK/AU markets may push other platforms toward, validating the 'screen-time reduction as a rewarded, protective behavior' thesis and strengthening the case for school/brand partnerships positioning NOMO as a compliance-friendly alternative.

industry.headline: EU KIDS Act Proposal: Comprehensive Child-Safety Framework with Mandatory Age Verification
industry.source: Davis Wright Tremaine (DWT) Privacy & Security Law Blog
industry.summary: The EU's newly adopted KIDS Act would ban under-13 social media accounts, mandate zero-knowledge-proof age verification, and force account deactivations within six months, with fines up to 6% of global turnover. Though EU-specific, it intensifies the global regulatory wave NOMO's CEO is already engaging with in UK/US/AU policy circles, reinforcing demand for off-platform, reward-based alternatives.

reconsider.name: ScreenStrong
reconsider.reason: Not a true product/mechanic competitor — a school curriculum/procurement nonprofit rather than a screen-time reward app, weak fit vs. the app-block/rewards competitor bar.
reconsider.why_fits: Nonprofit being tapped for a proposed $17M+ South Carolina statewide digital wellness initiative for public/charter school students, showing it is actively competing for the same school/EdTech and state-level procurement relationships NOMO targets.

reconsider.name: CityPASS / Go City
reconsider.reason: Duplicate of the CityPASS entry already included.
reconsider.why_fits: CityPASS bundles discounted access to museums, landmarks and attractions across major US cities (Chicago, Boston, Seattle, New York, San Diego, etc.), directly matching the 'museum tickets, city green passes' reward criteria NOMO is seeking. reconsider.name: Illinois (SB 2427 bell-to-bell phone ban)
reconsider.reason: A state legislative mandate, not an actionable partner entity — better characterized as a regulatory/market signal than a GTM partner prospect.
reconsider.why_fits: Illinois just signed a statewide law requiring bell-to-bell cellphone restrictions in public schools starting 2027-2028, creating a fresh, large-scale procurement need for implementation partners across the state's districts.

reconsider.name: Little League Baseball / LLWS
reconsider.reason: Medium confidence; youth sports vertical adequately represented elsewhere; sponsorship signal not specific enough to NOMO's reward/GTM model.
reconsider.why_fits: Little League now runs a portfolio of 25+ Official Sponsors reaching roughly two million players and one million volunteers, and just launched a Fan Pass system built into its official app that gates prizes behind first-party fan registration — exactly the large-roster, app-embedded activation model NOMO could plug Moments/rewards into via the Youth Sports GTM vertical.

rejected_today.name: Foqos (and Switchly)
rejected_today.reason: Free/open-source NFC blocker trend in a region outside NOMO's priority markets ('Other'); marginal signal already captured by the broader app-block competitor category.
rejected_today.why_fits: A fresh wave of free/open-source NFC-based blockers is undercutting paid incumbents like Brick: <cite index="19-5">Foqos, a free, open-source iOS app from Canadian developer Ali Waseem, offers a polished alternative</cite>, while <cite index="19-2">Android users have Switchly, developed by Vienna-based Saltyy</cite> — new entrants worth tracking in NOMO's app-block competitive set.

rejected_today.name: Henrico County Public Schools (HCPS)

rejected_today.name: Las Virgenes Unified School District
rejected_today.reason: District explicitly wants to avoid gamified, engagement-driven apps — contradicts NOMO's gamified reward model, weak fit.
rejected_today.why_fits: The district is actively drafting new device-use regulations, with a board meeting where <cite index="23-4">district officials are seeking to minimize the time students spend on their screens while maximizing learning and achievement</cite> and explicitly flagging a desire to avoid gamified, engagement-driven apps — a timely, active-need account for NOMO's education-vertical outreach.

rejected_today.name: Kansas State Board of Education
rejected_today.reason: Redundant with Massachusetts and NYC district-policy stories already covering the phone-ban-driven GTM opportunity.
rejected_today.why_fits: <cite index="35-7">Kansas Governor Laura Kelly signed a statewide bell-to-bell cell phone ban on March 20, 2026, applying to all public and accredited nonpublic K-12 schools and requiring districts to certify compliance to the Kansas State Board of Education by September 1, 2026.</cite> The imminent compliance deadline creates urgent district-level demand for an engagement/enforcement and positive-incentive tool like NOMO, fitting the 6-12 Education direct GTM vertical.

rejected_today.name: Dave & Buster's
rejected_today.reason: Same underlying Dallas Teen All-Access Pass story as State Fair of Texas; lower confidence, cut as duplicate.

Arcade/game-credit experiences are a genuine gap versus NOMO's current lineup of concerts, sports tickets, and apparel, and as a national chain it offers realistic, scalable tradeable inventory (game cards/credits) for a teen audience.
